== Biography ==
Robert is currently recorded as born about 1724 and attached as a son of [[Glasgow-1025|James Glasgow]] and [[Rutherford-4861|Margaret Rutherford]]. The only cited basis is a user-contributed FamilySearch tree; no inspected original record yet proves his birth, parents, migration or death.

== Research Notes ==
=== Moneymore place conflict ===

The structured birthplace “Moneymore, County Galway” combines a real place-name with a county that does not fit the Moneymore used in this family reconstruction. Moneymore in Artrea civil parish is in County Londonderry, not County Galway.<ref>[https://www.townlands.ie/londonderry/loughinsholin/artrea/moneymore/moneymore/ Townlands.ie, “Moneymore Townland, Co. Londonderry”], placing Moneymore in Artrea civil parish, barony of Loughinsholin, County Londonderry.</ref> This geographic correction does '''not''' prove that Robert was born in the Londonderry townland: several Irish places share the name, and no record inspected for Robert identifies one of them.

PRONI's official church-register guide lists First Moneymore Presbyterian baptisms only from 1827, Second Moneymore from 1845, and Ardtrea/Desertlin Roman Catholic baptisms from 1832.<ref>[https://www.proni.gov.uk/publications/proni-guide-church-records Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, ''Guide to Church Records''], First Moneymore Presbyterian MIC1P/339; Second Moneymore Presbyterian MIC1P/340; Ardtrea/Desertlin MIC1D/35 and T3050; guide consulted 30 August 2026.</ref> None of those surviving series can record a birth about 1724. This explains the register gap but does not prove Robert's identity, birthplace or parents; deeds, estate papers, probate and other contemporary records remain the appropriate next search.

The current parents, sibling group, birth and death locations are retained until evidence supplies replacements. They should be treated as unproved tree claims, as noted in [[Space:Glasgow Branches in Early Ireland|Glasgow Branches in Early Ireland]], rather than silently cleared or converted into a different family.

=== Possible Robert Glasgow, Cecil County plantation notice, 1786 ===
A notice dated North Susquehanna hundred, Cecil county, Maryland, 10 February 1786 offers a 260-acre plantation for public vendue on 10 March, with immediate possession given by Robert Glasgow and Joshua Hartshorn.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/41024006/ The Pennsylvania Gazette, 1786-02-15, p.1].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/41024088/ The Pennsylvania Gazette, 1786-03-01, p.4].</ref>

The two issues advertise one planned sale. Robert’s role as owner, agent or another participant is not specified; the notice proves neither a completed sale nor kinship with Joshua Hartshorn.

This may concern [[Glasgow-2425]]. Estimated birth c. 1724 in Ireland and death place United States leave the chronology possible, but the known account gives no Maryland residence or relevant occupation. The identification is therefore weak.
